title: On Inverse Theorems and Combinatorial Lines
authors: Amey Bhangale (University of California, USA), Subhash Khot (New York University, USA), Yang P. Liu (Carnegie Mellon University, USA), Dor Minzer (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, USA)
abstract: We study k-wise correlations in product spaces, i.e., correlations of the form $\mathrm{E}_{(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\sim \mu^{\otimes n}}[\,f_1(x_1)\·s f_k(x_k)\,]$, where each $f_i$ is a $1$-bounded function on $\Sigma_i^n$ and $\mu$ is a distribution over $\Sigma_1\times\·s\times\Sigma_k$. These correlations arise in additive and extremal combinatorics, hardness of approximation, and probability. The goal in an inverse theorem is to characterize the functions $f_1,\ldots,f_k$ that achieve nontrivial correlations under minimal assumptions on $\mu$. We give new inverse theorems for k-wise correlations for all $k\ge 3$. For $k=3$, our inverse theorem works for any pairwise-connected distribution $\mu$, which is essentially the minimal assumption required for a nontrivial inverse theorem to hold. For $k>3$, our inverse theorem applies to distributions $\mu$ that do not admit any Abelian embeddings, resolving a conjecture from [Bhangale--Khot--Minzer, STOC 2022]. We give applications to additive combinatorics, hardness of approximation, and property testing. First, there exists $c>0$ such that any set $A\subseteq \{0,1,2\}^n$ with density at least $\Omega((\log\log\log\log n)^{-c})$ must contain a combinatorial line: there exist $x,y,z\in\{0,1,2\}^n$, not all equal, such that for every $i=1,2,\ldots,n$, either $x_i=y_i=z_i$ or $(x_i,y_i,z_i)=(0,1,2)$. In other words, we obtain "reasonable bounds" for the density Hales-Jewett theorem of length $3$. This involves combining our inverse theorems with additional insights, motivated by Shkredov's proof of the corners theorem and Polymath's combinatorial proof of the density Hales-Jewett theorem. Second, we show how to construct a dictatorship-vs-quasirandom test that has perfect completeness and soundness $s+\epsilon$ from integrality gap instances with similar parameters, provided that the associated local distributions have no Abelian embeddings. Third, we analyze the direct-sum tester of [Dinur--Golubev, RANDOM 2019] in the low-soundness regime.
